title: This Bird Flies the Length of the Planet Twice a Year, in a Zigzag
subject: Arctic tern

scenes.text: One bird flies from the top of the world to the bottom and back every year.
In 2010, scientists tracked Arctic terns from Greenland with tiny devices. They flew about forty-four thousand miles a year.
Greenland to the Weddell Sea off Antarctica, and all the way back.
Not in a straight line. Winds pushed them into a giant S-shape, thousands of kilometers longer.
The detour saves energy, because the winds do the work. Over a lifetime, that adds up to about three trips to the Moon and back.
The longer route is the easier one.

description:
Arctic terns fly about 44,000 miles a year from Greenland to Antarctica and back.
They zigzag on purpose to ride the winds, and over a lifetime it adds up to about three trips to the Moon.
Would you take the longer, easier route?
